sections.purpose: To count blood cells (RBC, WBC) or microbial cells accurately using a Neubauer haemocytometer as per standard pharmacological and clinical practices.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacology laboratory for blood cell counting experiments and clinical pharmacology practicals.
procedure: Clean the haemocytometer chamber and coverslip thoroughly with 70% ethanol and wipe dry with lens paper.
Place the coverslip over the counting chamber and press gently until Newton's rings are visible at the edges.
Prepare blood dilution as per requirement: for RBC count dilute 1:200 with Hayem's solution; for WBC count dilute 1:20 with Turk's fluid.
Mix the diluted sample thoroughly by rotating the mixing vial for 2 minutes.
Discard the first 3–4 drops from the pipette tip.
Touch the tip of the pipette to the edge of the coverslip and allow the chamber to fill by capillary action — do not overfill.
Allow the cells to settle for 2–3 minutes before counting.
Place the haemocytometer under the microscope and focus using low power (10×), then switch to high power (40×) for counting.
For RBC: Count cells in the central square (5 small squares × 16 = 80 smallest squares); For WBC: Count cells in all 4 corner squares.
Apply standard counting rule: count cells touching the top and right boundaries; exclude cells touching bottom and left boundaries.
Record cell counts and apply appropriate formula to calculate cells per mm³.
Clean the haemocytometer immediately after use with distilled water followed by 70% ethanol.
Document results in the practical record book.
precautions: Ensure the haemocytometer and coverslip are grease-free before use.
Do not overfill or underfill the counting chamber.
Allow adequate settling time before counting to ensure cells are in focus.
Wear gloves when handling blood samples; follow universal precautions.
Dispose of all blood-contaminated materials in biohazard waste containers.
Calibrate the microscope and verify the ruling before use.
Avoid using cracked or scratched haemocytometers.
